Is the escape character fixed or configurable? Maybe we should use "Verify that the application uses escape characters (usually backslashes) to escape".

Note I removed the word "correctly", as it does not add anything.

edit: the updated proposal
> Verify that the application uses escape characters (usually backslash) to escape special characters being used in regular expressions to ensure they are not misinterpreted as metacharacters.

Is the escape character fixed or configurable? Maybe we should use "Verify that the application uses escape characters (usually backslashes) to escape".

Note I removed the word "correctly", as it does not add anything.

The backslash is fixed in most languages. (Java, C#, JavaScript, Python) But there are edge cases like POSIX extended RegEx and some libraries do this automatically. I like Elar's modification. I have a small change suggestion:

 _Verify that the application escapes special characters in regular expressions (typically using a backslash) to prevent them from being misinterpreted as metacharacters._

The backslash is fixed in most languages. (Java, C#, JavaScript, Python) But there are edge cases like POSIX extended RegEx and some libraries do this automatically. I like Elar's modification.
